rounds.text: Shivalic Power Control Ltd presents severe fundamental and technical deterioration despite a deceptively low headline P/E of 16.2x [E1]. Trailing twelve-month profit growth has collapsed to -17% [E13], driven by a sharp contraction in operating margins down to 9% in Mar 2026 from 18% in the year-ago quarter [E19]. Most alarming is the total breakdown in cash generation, evidenced by a cash conversion of -1.80x, operating cash flow plunging to negative Rs -18 Cr, and free cash flow dropping to negative Rs -20 Cr in Mar 2026 [E22, E23, E24]. This cash drain has forced borrowings up sharply from Rs 5 Cr to Rs 28 Cr within a single year [E27]. Meanwhile, smart money is fleeing: foreign and domestic institutions have drastically slashed their holdings from 4.88% and 7.11% down to 0.54% and 0.49% respectively since Jun 2024 [E30, E31]. The stock suffers from extreme technical weakness, resting at a relative strength rating of 0, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and yielding a miserable Sharpe ratio of -1.19 [E38, E39, E43]. Conceded: [E33] A discounted cash flow model suggests a higher intrinsic value and substantial margin of safety based on base-case assumptions.

Conceded: [E13, E19, E22, E23, E24, E27, E30, E31, E38, E39, E43]. While the bear highlights severe short-term earnings and cash flow pressures in Mar 2026, the long-term compounding profile shows an established 5-year sales growth of 22% and a 5-year profit growth of 73% [E8, E11]. The stock trades at an attractive P/E of 16.2x and a price-to-book value of just 1.36x on a book value of 51.1 [E1, E2]. Furthermore, debt remains conservative at 0.23x equity even after the recent rise in borrowings [E26, E27]. Promoters have actually increased their stake slightly to 71.34%, signaling confidence from insiders who know the business best [E29]. A rigorous discounted cash flow model values the company at Rs 168 per share, creating a substantial margin of safety of 58.7% at the current market price [E33, E34]. The reverse DCF demonstrates that the market price only prices in a modest 5.8% earnings growth, which is well below the base-case expectation of 18.0% [E35].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E8, E11, E26, E29, E33, E34, E35]. The bull's reliance on historical 5-year sales and profit growth ignores the severe collapse happening right now, evidenced by a trailing twelve month profit growth of -17% and a quarterly net profit decline of -38% YoY [E13, E53]. While debt-to-equity is reported at 0.23x, borrowings jumped significantly to Rs 28 Cr in Mar 2026 from just Rs 5 Cr a year earlier, coinciding with operating cash flow crashing to Rs -18 Cr and free cash flow dropping to Rs -20 Cr [E23, E24, E27]. This negative cash conversion of -1.80x means reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual cash generation [E22]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is non-existent: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have plummeted heavily, matching a negative money flow signal and an RS rating of 0 where the stock sits 42.4% away from its 52-week high below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E30, E31, E32, E37, E38, E39]. Finally, the rules-based screen scores the business at a lowly 37 out of 100 with a SELL rating, confirming that theoretical DCF upside fails to account for deteriorating margins, negative cash flows, and aggressive institutional exit [E37, E48].
